title: Showcase & tests
text:
An animated Turtle graphics widget for Jupyter, built on anywidget so it renders identically in VS Code, JupyterLab, Notebook 7, and Colab. Each cell below draws something and animates it on an HTML canvas. Pass show_code=True to display the cell’s source beside the canvas and highlight each line in sync with the drawing. Use the Replay/Pause buttons under any canvas.
from turtle_widget import Turtle

title: Showcase & tests
text:
1. The basics
A turtle starts at the centre (0, 0) facing east (heading 0). forward/backward move it, left/right rotate it (degrees, counter-clockwise positive). Here’s a square.

t = Turtle()
t.speed(6)
for _ in range(4):
    t.forward(120)
    t.left(90)





t = Turtle(show_code=True)
t.speed(1)
colours = ["red", "blue", "yellow", "brown", "black", "purple", "green"]

t.penup(); t.left(90); t.forward(200); t.right(90); t.pendown()
for i in range(0, 18):
    t.pencolor(colours[i % 7])
    t.right(20)
    t.forward(50)

t.right(180)
t.home()

2. Synced code highlighting (show_code=True)
With show_code=True, the source appears on the right and the active line is highlighted as the animation reaches it.

t = Turtle(show_code=True)
t.speed(2)
for _ in range(4):
    t.forward(120)
    t.left(90)





t = Turtle(show_code=True)
t.speed(1)
colours = ["red", "blue", "yellow", "brown", "black", "purple", "green"]

t.penup(); t.left(90); t.forward(200); t.right(90); t.pendown()
for i in range(0, 18):
    t.pencolor(colours[i % 7])
    t.right(20)
    t.forward(50)

t.right(180)
t.home()

title: Showcase & tests
text:
3. Colors, pen width & fills
Colours accept CSS names ("gold"), hex ("#ff8800"), or RGB tuples ((0.1, 0.5, 0.9) on the 0–1 scale, or (255, 128, 0) on the 0–255 scale). Wrap a path in begin_fill() / end_fill() to fill it — the fill lands behind the outline, just like real turtle.

t = Turtle()
t.speed(8)
t.pensize(3)
t.pencolor("#d2691e")          # outline
t.fillcolor((1.0, 0.84, 0.0))  # gold, on the 0-1 RGB scale
t.begin_fill()
for _ in range(5):             # classic 5-point star
    t.forward(220)
    t.right(144)
t.end_fill()

title: Showcase & tests
text:
4. Circles & arcs
circle(radius) draws a full circle to the left of the turtle; a negative radius goes right. circle(radius, extent) draws only part of it. Stacking rotated circles gives a spirograph.

t = Turtle()
t.speed(10)
palette = ["crimson", "darkorange", "seagreen", "royalblue", "purple", "teal"]
for i in range(12):
    t.right(5)
    for i in range(12):    
        t.pencolor(palette[i % len(palette)])
        t.circle(90)
        t.right(30)

title: Showcase & tests
text:
5. Dots, stamps, text & jumps
penup() / pendown() lift and drop the pen so you can jump without drawing. dot(size) plants a filled dot, stamp() leaves a copy of the turtle, and write(text) prints a label.

t = Turtle(width=520, height=320)
t.speed(7)

t.penup(); t.goto(-210, 30); t.pendown()
for i, c in enumerate(["red", "orange", "green", "blue", "purple"]):
    t.dot(16 + i * 8, c)
    t.penup(); t.forward(90); t.pendown()

t.penup(); t.goto(-210, 90); t.pendown()
t.pencolor("black")
t.write("dots grow to the right", font=("sans-serif", 16, "normal"))

t.penup(); t.goto(0, -70); t.setheading(60); t.pendown()
t.pencolor("seagreen")
t.stamp()

34

title: Showcase & tests
text:
6. Speed & instant mode
speed(1) is slowest, speed(10) is fastest, and speed(0) disables animation entirely — the whole drawing appears at once, which is handy for dense figures. (Word forms also work: "slowest", "slow", "normal", "fast", "fastest".)

t = Turtle()
t.speed(0)               # no animation: drawn instantly
# t.speed(10)
t.pencolor("teal")
t.pensize(1)
for _ in range(72):
    t.forward(160)
    t.left(175)          # a dense star spiral
t.hideturtle()

title: Showcase & tests
text:
7. Reading turtle state
Getters return the current state without drawing anything: pos(), xcor(), ycor(), heading(), isdown(), isvisible(). (Use autoshow=False when you only want to inspect state and not render a widget.)

probe = Turtle(autoshow=False)
probe.forward(100); probe.left(90); probe.forward(50)
print("position:", probe.pos())
print("heading :", probe.heading())
print("pen down:", probe.isdown())

position: (100.0, 50.0)
heading : 90.0
pen down: True

title: Showcase & tests
text:
8. Sensing obstacles
The turtle can sense obstacles: registered shapes (add_circle, add_rectangle, add_segment, add_polygon), its own drawn trail, and the canvas edges.

distance_ahead() casts a ray along the heading and returns the distance to the first obstacle (or None).
sense(max_distance=...) returns every obstacle within range, nearest first, each with the distance and the signed angle (degrees, + = left) to its closest point.
nearest() is just the closest one.

Pass draw=True to any of them to overlay the sensor rays on the canvas.

from turtle_widget import Turtle

t = Turtle()
t.speed(5)

def on_hit(c): 
    t.penup(); t.goto(c.point); t.pencolor("red");
    t.right(180+2*c.angle, speed=0)
    t.pendown();  
    t.dot(15) 
    t.pencolor("black")
    t.forward(c.speed)
 
t.on_collision(on_hit) 
t.add_circle(120, 60, 35)
t.add_rectangle(-180, -120, -80, 60)
t.add_segment(40, -160, 200, -40)
# t.hide_obstacles()
# t.show_obstacles()  

for i in range(300):
    d = t.distance_ahead(draw=True, trail=False)
    d.distance
    for d in t.sense(max_distance=200, draw=True, color='gray'):
        d.angle

title: Showcase & tests
text:
9. Self-test (headless)
Geometry is computed in Python, so it can be validated without a browser. This cell asserts a few invariants and checks the event stream is JSON-serializable (which is what gets sent to the frontend).

import json
from turtle_widget import Turtle

# movement + heading
t = Turtle(autoshow=False)
t.forward(100); t.left(90); t.forward(100)
assert abs(t.xcor() - 100) < 1e-9, t.xcor()
assert abs(t.ycor() - 100) < 1e-9, t.ycor()
assert round(t.heading() % 360, 6) == 90

# home returns to origin, heading 0
t.home()
assert abs(t.xcor()) < 1e-9 and abs(t.ycor()) < 1e-9
assert round(t.heading() % 360, 6) == 0

# circle returns (approximately) to its start
c = Turtle(autoshow=False)
c.begin_fill(); c.circle(60); c.end_fill()
assert abs(c.xcor()) < 1e-6 and abs(c.ycor()) < 1e-6
assert any(e["op"] == "fill" for e in c._events)

# every event is JSON-serializable and carries a source line + speed
payload = json.dumps(t._events)
assert all("line" in e and "speed" in e for e in t._events)

print("All self-tests passed.")
print("square+home events:", len(t._events), "| circle events:", len(c._events))

All self-tests passed.
square+home events: 5 | circle events: 23

title: Turtle
text:
turtle_widget.Turtle(
    width=500,
    height=500,
    show_code=False,
    code=None,
    autoshow=True,
    bg='white',
    home=None,
)
An animated, turtle-compatible drawing widget for Jupyter notebooks.
Turtle commands are recorded in Python as a stream of events and replayed as a canvas animation below the cell. The widget displays itself automatically at the end of the cell; you can also call show() or evaluate the turtle to display it.



width : int = 500

Canvas width in pixels. Default 500.

height : int = 500

Canvas height in pixels. Default 500.

show_code : bool = False

If True, show the cell source beside the canvas and highlight the active line in sync with the animation. Default False.

code : str = None

Source to display instead of the captured cell source.

autoshow : bool = True

If True (default), display the widget automatically at the end of the cell. Set False for headless use such as tests.

bg : str = 'white'

Canvas background colour. Default "white".

home : tuple of float = None

The turtle’s home, given as (x, y) or (x, y, heading) (heading defaults to 0; 0 = east). Defaults to the origin (0, 0) facing east. The turtle both starts here and returns here on :func:home. (To re-target the home of an existing turtle without moving it, call :func:sethome.)






nr_collisions : int

Running count of collisions detected since the turtle was created (reset to 0 by :func:reset). Incremented once per collision reported while an :func:on_collision handler is active — so with the default stop=True it counts the obstacles the turtle has run into, and with stop=False every crossing reported. Starts at 0.

nr_left, nr_right : int

Number of times :func:left / :func:right has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:reset. (The aliases lt/rt count too, as they are the same methods.)

nr_sense, nr_distance_ahead : int

Number of times :func:sense / :func:distance_ahead has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:reset. nearest is not counted (it does not call sense).

total_movement : float

Total distance the turtle has travelled, in turtle units, summed over every move (forward/backward/goto/circle/home/…), whether the pen is up or down. A move stopped short by a collision contributes only the distance actually travelled; turns contribute nothing. Starts at 0.0, reset by :func:reset.








Name
Description




add_circle
Register a circular obstacle and draw it.


add_polygon
Register a filled polygon obstacle and draw it.


add_rectangle
Register a rectangular obstacle (a 4-point polygon) and draw it.


add_segment
Register a line-segment (wall) obstacle and draw it.


backward
Move the turtle backward by distance (opposite its heading).


begin_fill
Start recording a filled shape.


bgcolor
Get or set the canvas background colour.


circle
Draw a circle or arc, approximated by a series of straight chords.


clear
Clear the drawing and the sensed trail from the canvas.


color
Get or set the pen colour, the fill colour, or both at once.


distance_ahead
Sense the nearest obstacle straight ahead.


dot
Draw a filled dot at the current position.


duration
Total time the animation will take to play, in seconds.


end_fill
Fill the shape traced since the last begin_fill.


fillcolor
Get or set the fill colour used by begin_fill / end_fill.


forward
Move the turtle forward by distance, drawing if the pen is down.


goto
Move the turtle to an absolute position, drawing if the pen is down.


heading
Return the current heading in degrees.


hide_obstacles
Hide all registered obstacles from view.


hideturtle
Hide the turtle marker.


home
Move the turtle to its home position and turn to the home heading.


isdown
Return whether the pen is down.


isvisible
Return whether the turtle marker is visible.


left
Turn the turtle counter-clockwise by angle degrees.


nearest
The single nearest obstacle within range, or None.


on_collision
Register a hook fired when a move runs into an obstacle.


pencolor
Get or set the pen (outline) colour.


pendown
Lower the pen so subsequent moves draw.


pensize
Get or set the pen width.


penup
Lift the pen so subsequent moves do not draw.


position
Return the current position.


reset
Clear the drawing and reset the turtle to its initial state.


right
Turn the turtle clockwise by angle degrees.


sense
Detect all obstacles within range, with the bearing to each.


setheading
Turn the turtle to face an absolute heading.


sethome
Set the home position that :func:home returns to.


setx
Set the x-coordinate, keeping y unchanged.


sety
Set the y-coordinate, keeping x unchanged.


show
Flush the recorded commands and display the widget now.


show_obstacles
Make all registered obstacles visible.


showturtle
Make the turtle marker visible.


speed
Get or set the drawing speed.


stamp
Stamp a copy of the turtle shape at the current position and heading.


write
Write text at the current position.


xcor
Return the current x-coordinate.


ycor
Return the current y-coordinate.





turtle_widget.Turtle.add_circle(
    x,
    y,
    radius,
    color=None,
    visible=True,
    label=None,
    sense=True,
)
Register a circular obstacle and draw it.



x : float

Centre of the circle, in turtle coordinates.

y : float

Centre of the circle, in turtle coordinates.

radius : float

Radius of the circle.

color : str or tuple = None

Outline/fill colour. Defaults to a neutral obstacle colour.

visible : bool = True

Whether to draw it (default True). Invisible obstacles are still sensed and still collide.

label : str = None

A name carried on the obstacle and surfaced as .label on the Detection/Collision objects that report it. Not drawn.

sense : bool = True

Whether distance_ahead/sense/nearest can detect it (default True). A non-sensing obstacle is still drawn (unless visible=False) and still collides — it is only hidden from the sensing queries.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.

    points,
    color=None,
    visible=True,
    label=None,
    sense=True,
)
Register a filled polygon obstacle and draw it.

Polygon vertices in turtle coordinates; the last vertex is joined back to the first.

Outline/fill colour. Defaults to a neutral obstacle colour.

Whether to draw it (default True). Invisible obstacles are still sensed and still collide.

A name carried on the obstacle and surfaced as .label on the Detection/Collision objects that report it. Not drawn.

sense : bool = True

Whether distance_ahead/sense/nearest can detect it (default True). A non-sensing obstacle is still drawn (unless visible=False) and still collides — it is only hidden from the sensing queries.






 : Turtle

One corner of the rectangle.

One corner of the rectangle.

The opposite corner.

sense : bool = True

Whether distance_ahead/sense/nearest can detect it (default True). A non-sensing obstacle is still drawn (unless visible=False) and still collides — it is only hidden from the sensing queries.

Register a line-segment (wall) obstacle and draw it.



x1 : float

One endpoint of the segment.

y1 : float

One endpoint of the segment.

x2 : float

The other endpoint.

y2 : float

The other endpoint.

color : str or tuple = None

Segment colour. Defaults to a neutral obstacle colour.

visible : bool = True

Whether to draw it (default True). Invisible obstacles are still sensed and still collide.

label : str = None

A name carried on the obstacle and surfaced as .label on the Detection/Collision objects that report it. Not drawn.

sense : bool = True

Whether distance_ahead/sense/nearest can detect it (default True). A non-sensing obstacle is still drawn (unless visible=False) and still collides — it is only hidden from the sensing queries.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.backward(distance, speed=1.0)
Move the turtle backward by distance (opposite its heading).



distance : float

Distance to move opposite the current heading.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.begin_fill()
Start recording a filled shape.
Call before the commands that trace the outline, then call end_fill to fill it.



 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.bgcolor(*args)
Get or set the canvas background colour.



*args :  = ()

A CSS colour name/hex string or an (r, g, b) triple. With no arguments, the current background colour is returned.






 : Turtle or str

This turtle when setting (to allow chaining), or the current background colour when called with no arguments.






turtle_widget.Turtle.circle(radius, extent=None, steps=None, speed=1.0)
Draw a circle or arc, approximated by a series of straight chords.
A positive radius curves to the left of the turtle, a negative radius to the right.



radius : float

Radius of the circle. Positive curves left, negative curves right.

extent : float = None

Angle of the arc to draw, in degrees. Defaults to 360 (a full circle).

steps : int = None

Number of chords approximating the arc. Defaults to a value scaled to the radius and extent.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.clear()
Clear the drawing and the sensed trail from the canvas.
Registered obstacles are kept (they are redrawn); the turtle’s position, heading and pen are unchanged.



 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.color(*args)
Get or set the pen colour, the fill colour, or both at once.



*args :  = ()

With no arguments, returns (pencolor, fillcolor). With one argument, sets both pen and fill to that colour. With two, sets the pen and fill colours respectively. Each colour may be a CSS name/hex string or an (r, g, b) triple.






 : Turtle or tuple of str

This turtle when setting (to allow chaining), or the (pencolor, fillcolor) pair when called with no arguments.






turtle_widget.Turtle.distance_ahead(
    max_distance=None,
    walls=True,
    trail=True,
    draw=False,
    color='red',
)
Sense the nearest obstacle straight ahead.
Casts a ray from the turtle along its current heading and returns the first obstacle it hits as a Detection — the same object :func:sense yields. Increments nr_distance_ahead.



max_distance : float = None

Ignore hits farther than this. None (default) means unlimited.

walls : bool = True

Include the canvas border as an obstacle. Default True.

trail : bool = True

Include the turtle’s own drawn path as obstacles. Default True.

draw : bool = False

If True, also draw the sensor ray on the canvas. Default False.

color : str or tuple = 'red'

Colour of the drawn ray, used only when draw=True. Default "red"; accepts a CSS colour string or an (r, g, b) tuple.






 : Detection or None

The nearest obstacle ahead, with the same fields as a sense result — distance, angle (the signed angle of incidence — 0 = head-on, ±90 = grazing), point, obstacle (the shape hit), kind and index — or None if nothing is within range.






turtle_widget.Turtle.dot(size=None, *color)
Draw a filled dot at the current position.



size : float = None

Diameter of the dot in pixels. Defaults to a small multiple of the pen size.

*color :  = ()

Optional dot colour as a CSS name/hex string or an (r, g, b) triple. Defaults to the current pen colour.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.duration()
Total time the animation will take to play, in seconds.
Computed from the recorded events using the exact timing the browser uses: a line/move of length d at effective speed s takes d / (s * 150) seconds, a turn of a degrees takes a / (s * 180) seconds, and every other event (dots, stamps, writes, fills, pen/colour changes, sensing, …) is instant. A move whose effective speed is 0 is instant too — it snaps into place. The effective speed already includes any per-move speed= multiplier.



 : float

Seconds the full animation will take at the current events’ speeds. 0.0 if speed is 0 (everything is instant) or nothing has been drawn yet.





This is the scheduled play time derived from the event stream — it excludes the browser’s frame-scheduling overhead and does not change as the animation plays. The currently elapsed time lives in the browser; the Python Turtle records events but does not receive playback progress back, so live elapsed/remaining time is not readable here. turtle_widget.Turtle.on_collision(handler, stop=True, walls=True, trail=False)
Register a hook fired when a move runs into an obstacle.
Collision detection is opt-in — calling this enables it; until then moves are unaffected. By default the turtle stops at the first obstacle (or canvas edge) it hits: the move is shortened to the contact point and the turtle ends there. After a move that hit something, handler(collision) is called with the contact details; the handler may then issue ordinary turtle commands (which animate next) to react. Each reported collision also increments the turtle’s nr_collisions counter.



handler : callable or None

Called as handler(collision) with a Collision (see Notes). Pass None to turn collision detection off again.

stop : bool = True

If True (default), the turtle stops at the first contact. If False, motion is unchanged (the move completes) and the handler is notified for every obstacle the path crossed, nearest first.

walls : bool = True

Treat the canvas border as an obstacle. Default True.

trail : bool = False

Also collide with the turtle’s own drawn path (self-collision). Default False.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.





Each Collision carries the contact point (x, y); the obstacle that was hit (an Obstacle exposing .kind — "circle"/"segment"/"polygon"/"wall"/"trail" — plus .label and its geometry); its index among registered obstacles (else None); the unit surface normal at the contact, facing back toward the turtle (reflect a direction d with d - 2*(d·n)*n to bounce); the distance travelled into the move; angle, the signed angle of incidence in degrees (0 = a head-on, perpendicular hit; ±90 = a grazing hit parallel to the surface; the sign distinguishes the two glancing sides); speed, the effective animation speed of the move (global speed() × the move’s speed= multiplier); and the turtle’s state — pos, heading, isdown, isvisible, pencolor, pensize. The handler’s own moves do not re-trigger collisions, so it can move the turtle freely (e.g. to bounce or back away).

title: Turtle
text:
width : int = 500

Canvas width in pixels. Default 500.

height : int = 500

Canvas height in pixels. Default 500.

show_code : bool = False

If True, show the cell source beside the canvas and highlight the active line in sync with the animation. Default False.

code : str = None

Source to display instead of the captured cell source.

autoshow : bool = True

If True (default), display the widget automatically at the end of the cell. Set False for headless use such as tests.

bg : str = 'white'

Canvas background colour. Default "white".

home : tuple of float = None

The turtle’s home, given as (x, y) or (x, y, heading) (heading defaults to 0; 0 = east). Defaults to the origin (0, 0) facing east. The turtle both starts here and returns here on :func:home. (To re-target the home of an existing turtle without moving it, call :func:sethome.)

title: Turtle
text:
nr_collisions : int

Running count of collisions detected since the turtle was created (reset to 0 by :func:reset). Incremented once per collision reported while an :func:on_collision handler is active — so with the default stop=True it counts the obstacles the turtle has run into, and with stop=False every crossing reported. Starts at 0.

nr_left, nr_right : int

Number of times :func:left / :func:right has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:reset. (The aliases lt/rt count too, as they are the same methods.)

nr_sense, nr_distance_ahead : int

Number of times :func:sense / :func:distance_ahead has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:reset. nearest is not counted (it does not call sense).

total_movement : float

Total distance the turtle has travelled, in turtle units, summed over every move (forward/backward/goto/circle/home/…), whether the pen is up or down. A move stopped short by a collision contributes only the distance actually travelled; turns contribute nothing. Starts at 0.0, reset by :func:reset.

This is the scheduled play time derived from the event stream — it excludes the browser’s frame-scheduling overhead and does not change as the animation plays. turtle_widget.Turtle.isdown()
Return whether the pen is down.



 : bool

True if the pen is down (drawing), False otherwise.






turtle_widget.Turtle.isvisible()
Return whether the turtle marker is visible.



 : bool

True if the turtle marker is shown, False otherwise.






turtle_widget.Turtle.left(angle, speed=1.0)
Turn the turtle counter-clockwise by angle degrees.
The animation spins exactly angle degrees, so multi-turn values such as left(720) are preserved as two full rotations. Increments nr_left.



angle : float

Degrees to turn counter-clockwise.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.nearest(
    max_distance=None,
    walls=True,
    trail=True,
    draw=False,
    color='red',
)
The single nearest obstacle within range, or None.
A convenience wrapper around :func:sense returning only the closest detection.



max_distance : float = None

Only consider obstacles within this distance. None (default) considers every obstacle.

walls : bool = True

Include the canvas border. Default True.

trail : bool = True

Include the turtle’s own drawn path. Default True.

draw : bool = False

If True, draw a ray to the nearest detected point. Default False.

color : str or tuple = 'red'

Colour of the drawn ray, used only when draw=True. Default "red"; accepts a CSS colour string or an (r, g, b) tuple.






 : Detection or None

The nearest detection (see sense), or None if nothing is within range.






turtle_widget.Turtle.on_collision(handler, stop=True, walls=True, trail=False)
Register a hook fired when a move runs into an obstacle.
Collision detection is opt-in — calling this enables it; until then moves are unaffected. By default the turtle stops at the first obstacle (or canvas edge) it hits: the move is shortened to the contact point and the turtle ends there. After a move that hit something, handler(collision) is called with the contact details; the handler may then issue ordinary turtle commands (which animate next) to react. Each reported collision also increments the turtle’s nr_collisions counter.



handler : callable or None

Called as handler(collision) with a Collision (see Notes). Pass None to turn collision detection off again.

stop : bool = True

If True (default), the turtle stops at the first contact. If False, motion is unchanged (the move completes) and the handler is notified for every obstacle the path crossed, nearest first.

walls : bool = True

Treat the canvas border as an obstacle. Default True.

trail : bool = False

Also collide with the turtle’s own drawn path (self-collision). Default False.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.





Each Collision carries the contact point (x, y); the obstacle that was hit (an Obstacle exposing .kind — "circle"/"segment"/"polygon"/"wall"/"trail" — plus .label and its geometry); its index among registered obstacles (else None); the unit surface normal at the contact, facing back toward the turtle (reflect a direction d with d - 2*(d·n)*n to bounce); the distance travelled into the move; angle, the signed angle of incidence in degrees (0 = a head-on, perpendicular hit; ±90 = a grazing hit parallel to the surface; the sign distinguishes the two glancing sides); speed, the effective animation speed of the move (global speed() × the move’s speed= multiplier); and the turtle’s state — pos, heading, isdown, isvisible, pencolor, pensize. The handler’s own moves do not re-trigger collisions, so it can move the turtle freely (e.g. to bounce or back away).




turtle_widget.Turtle.pencolor(*args)
Get or set the pen (outline) colour.



*args :  = ()

A CSS colour name or hex string ("red", "#ff8800"), or an (r, g, b) triple given as three arguments or one tuple. Float components in [0, 1] use the 0-1 scale, otherwise 0-255.






 : Turtle or str

This turtle when setting (to allow chaining), or the current pen colour when called with no arguments.






turtle_widget.Turtle.pendown()
Lower the pen so subsequent moves draw.



 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.pensize(width=None)
Get or set the pen width.



width : float = None

New pen width in pixels. If omitted, the current width is returned.






 : Turtle or float

This turtle when setting (to allow chaining), or the current pen width when called with no argument.





Named pensize (alias width_) because width is the canvas-size trait.




turtle_widget.Turtle.penup()
Lift the pen so subsequent moves do not draw.



 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.position()
Return the current position.



 : tuple of float

The (x, y) coordinates, with the origin at the canvas centre.

 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.right(angle, speed=1.0)
Turn the turtle clockwise by angle degrees.
The animation spins exactly angle degrees, so multi-turn values such as right(720) are preserved as two full rotations. Increments nr_right.



angle : float

Degrees to turn clockwise.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.sense(
    max_distance=None,
    walls=True,
    trail=True,
    draw=False,
    color='red',
)
Detect all obstacles within range, with the bearing to each.
For every obstacle whose closest point lies within max_distance of the turtle, returns a Detection giving the distance and the signed angle (relative to the turtle’s heading, positive = left / counter- clockwise) to that closest point. A point the turtle is touching is not reported. Increments nr_sense (nearest does not, since it does not call this method).



max_distance : float = None

Only report obstacles whose closest point is within this distance. None (default) reports every obstacle.

walls : bool = True

Include the canvas border. Default True.

trail : bool = True

Include the turtle’s own drawn path (its nearest point). Default True.

draw : bool = False

If True, also draw a ray to each detected point. Default False.

color : str or tuple = 'red'

Colour of the drawn rays, used only when draw=True. Default "red"; accepts a CSS colour string or an (r, g, b) tuple.






 : list of Detection

Detections sorted nearest-first. Each Detection has fields distance, angle (degrees), point (x, y), obstacle (the shape hit — an Obstacle exposing .kind/.label/geometry), kind (one of "circle", "segment", "polygon", "wall", "trail") and index (position among registered obstacles, else None).






turtle_widget.Turtle.setheading(to_angle, speed=1.0)
Turn the turtle to face an absolute heading.
Rotates along the shortest path, so turning from 0 to 270 spins -90 degrees rather than +270. Headings are in degrees with 0 = east, counter-clockwise positive.



to_angle : float

Absolute heading in degrees.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.sethome(x, y=None, heading=0)
Set the home position that :func:home returns to.
This does not move the turtle — it only redefines where home() goes; the turtle stays where it is. (To set home when creating the turtle, pass Turtle(home=(x, y)).)



x : float or tuple of float

Home x-coordinate, or an (x, y) / (x, y, heading) tuple (then y and heading must be omitted).

y : float = None

Home y-coordinate.

heading : float = 0

The heading (degrees, 0 = east) the turtle faces after home(). Default 0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.setx(x, speed=1.0)
Set the x-coordinate, keeping y unchanged.



x : float

New x-coordinate.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.sety(y, speed=1.0)
Set the y-coordinate, keeping x unchanged.



y : float

New y-coordinate.

speed : float = 1.0

Per-move multiplier on the global speed() (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.






 : Turtle

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.show()

This turtle, to allow method chaining.






turtle_widget.Turtle.speed(s=None)
Get or set the drawing speed.



s : int or str = None

Speed from 0 to 10, or a name: "fastest" (0), "fast" (10), "normal" (6), "slow" (3), "slowest" (1). 0 disables animation (the drawing appears at once). If omitted, the current speed is returned.

This turtle when setting (to allow chaining), or the current speed when called with no argument.

title: Overview
text:
turtle-widget is an animated, turtle-compatible drawing widget for Jupyter notebooks. You write ordinary turtle code in Python; the widget records each command and replays it as a smooth canvas animation right below the cell.
Built on anywidget, it behaves identically in VS Code, JupyterLab, Notebook 7, and Colab, and works offline.

title: Overview
text:
Installation

pixicondapip


pixi workspace channel add munch-group
pixi add turtle-widget


conda install -c munch-group turtle-widget


pip install turtle-widget




from turtle_widget import Turtle

t = Turtle()
t.speed(6)
for _ in range(4):     # a square
    t.forward(120)
    t.left(90)
